bull_bear.body: Prioritizing profitability over growth; No dividend or buyback mentioned; Strategic acquisitions (Planet Education Australia); Marketing spend on sports sponsorships (Big Cricket League, Kho Kho World Cup, WCL Season 2); No equity dilution planned for FY25 per promoter commitment
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Intense competition from private players burning cash; Air segment growth suppression due to discount cuts; Delayed hotel GBR growth despite seasonality; Promoter stake sales (though denied for FY25); Execution risk in international and corporate verticals; Regulatory risk in study tourism
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautious, defensive, and profit-focused; Management openly admits to sacrificing growth for margin; Confident in long-term sustainability; Repeatedly emphasizes bootstrapped heritage and avoidance of 'burn rate' competition; Tone is firm on discipline, slightly dismissive of competitor tactics
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Dubai growth is highly volatile (spurt-flat-spurts pattern) but management believes <5% of potential captured; Study tourism acquisition is a stealth play into high-margin, recurring education-travel ecosystem; Sports sponsorships (WCL Season 2: July-Aug 2025) are not just branding but direct customer acquisition channels
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deck's 'At a Glance' positioning states growth is funded by internal accruals, backed by strong cash flows and operational efficiency, with no mention of external debt/equity funding for expansion.
- FY26 consolidated cash and cash equivalents fell to Rs 802.2 Mn from Rs 1,361.5 Mn in FY25, and net cash from operating activities turned negative (Rs -951.0 Mn) on adverse working-capital changes, versus positive Rs 1,118.2 Mn in FY25.
- Total equity rose to Rs 8,149.2 Mn (FY26) from Rs 7,420.5 Mn (FY25); total borrowings remain small (~Rs 314.0 Mn FY26 vs ~Rs 348.1 Mn FY25), consistent with a low-leverage balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- brand: nearly two-decade brand built on a No Convenience Fee and Zero Hidden Cost model — evidence: "Over 17 years, EaseMyTrip has built one of India's most recognised travel brands with its No Convenience Fee and Zero Hidden Cost models serving as the foundation of deep customer trust"
- distribution: tri-channel distribution (B2C, B2B2C, B2E) with an agent/franchise network reaching Tier 2/3 cities — evidence: "The EMT Franchise model brings a physical presence to 39 stores across cities including Bhopal, Amritsar, and Karnal"
- scale: large registered user base and app footprint — evidence: "the platform has recorded over 21 million app downloads and serves a registered user base of more than 33 million"
- distribution: broad supplier integration in hotels — evidence: "Access to over 2.3 million hotels through direct/API integrations has significantly enriched the supplier network"
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economy risk — Operational and financial performance may be adversely affected by a contraction in the global economy or by disruptions impacting the Indian economy and its travel sector.
- Demand/seasonality risk — The Company is inherently susceptible to seasonal fluctuations within the travel and tourism industry; revenue tends to peak during summer and winter holiday seasons (Q1 and Q3), presenting a recurring challenge to consistent revenue generation.
- Competitive risk — EaseMyTrip operates within a highly competitive segment of the travel products and services industry, facing rivalry from established online travel agencies, traditional offline travel enterprises, diverse payment platforms, and search engines offering travel-related functionalities.
- Concentration risk — Significant reliance on airline ticketing as the primary revenue source constitutes a concentration risk; dependence on a single business vertical has the potential to affect revenue stability and margin performance during industry-specific downturns.
- Technological risk — The Company faces potential operational challenges should it fail to keep pace with the rapid evolution of technology, which could undermine operational efficiency and overall business performance.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Air: 86% of GBR (down from 97% at listing); Hotels: 10.6% of GBR (73% YoY growth in nights); Trains/Buses/Other: 2% of GBR (31.9% YoY growth); Dubai: INR 170cr GBR in Q3 (227% YoY growth); Study tourism: New via Planet Education Australia acquisition
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Competitors are growing faster by burning cash on discounts | Private OTAs (e.g., Yatra, MakeMyTrip private entities) | loser | Medium | EaseMyTrip's disciplined approach may lose market share short-term but could capture market when competitors' funding dries up |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Positions itself as India's Leading Online Travel Platform / OTA, founded in 2008, offering a One Stop Travel Ecosystem spanning flights, hotels, holiday packages, rail, bus, cab, charter, visa and ancillary services.
- Claims 90%+ customer repeat booking rate and 94.97% repeat transactions, cited as evidence of strong brand loyalty and trust.
- Differentiates via a tri-channel distribution model (B2C, B2B2C, B2E) and says it pioneered No Convenience Fee and Zero Hidden Cost pricing.
- Branded as an AI-Powered Travel platform ('AI-Led Innovation') offering personalized, hyper-tailored, cost-effective bookings.
- Describes growth as funded by internal accruals, framing a self-sustaining, low-leverage model versus typically VC/debt-funded OTA peers.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Nutana Aviation -- majority stake acquired in 2022, extending into aviation-adjacent services.
- [Acquisition] Dook Travels, Guideline Travels and Tripshope -- majority stakes acquired in 2023 as part of non-air segment expansion.
- [Corporate structure] Joined the 'Unicorn Club' and listed via IPO on NSE & BSE in 2021 (Scrip Code 543272 / Symbol EASEMYTRIP); incorporated EaseMyTrip Insurance Broker Pvt Ltd (majority stake) in 2024.
- [Board] Board comprises Chairman & MD Nishant Pitti and Director & CEO Rikant Pitti (co-founders), alongside independent directors with senior government/regulatory backgrounds -- ex-CBDT Member Neena Kumar, ex-CCI Director General Ajay Kumar Chauhan (IRS, Retd.), and ex-Indian Foreign Service High Commissioner Ruchi Ghanashyam.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: EaseMyTrip commenced operations in 2008 focused on the B2B2C segment, enabling travel agents across India to book domestic airline tickets and serve the offline travel market; it expanded into B2C in 2011 to serve India's growing middle class directly, and into B2E in 2013, offering end-to-end travel management solutions to corporate clients. The platform today offers an end-to-end travel product suite spanning flights, hotels, holidays, trains, buses, charters, cruises, activities, insurance and visas, distributed via websites, mobile apps and a wide travel-agent network, with international operations across the UAE, UK, USA, Singapore, Saudi Arabia and Brazil.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Air:** Domestic and international airline ticketing
- **Hotels & Holidays:** Hotel bookings, Holiday packages, Book at ₹0 (zero upfront payment hotel booking)
- **Non-air mobility:** YoloBus (intercity bus), Easy Green Mobility (EV mobility)
- **Hospitality management:** Spree Hospitality
- **Corporate/B2B:** EMTDesk (corporate travel & expense automation), EMTMate (agent/agency enablement tool)
- **Experiential/curated travel:** Explore Bharat, EasyDarshan (pilgrimage travel)
- **Ancillary:** Rail and bus ticketing, Travel insurance, Visa assistance, Car rentals

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Targeting FY2026 with 25% non-air contribution (from current 14%); Margin: Maintaining EBITDA margin >30%; Order inflow: No specific guidance; Capex/commissioning: No capex guidance disclosed
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: International expansion (Middle East, especially Dubai); Corporate travel digitization (AI-driven booking tools); Study tourism vertical; OLX and CARS24 partnerships; ONDC integration (mentioned but no update)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- EaseMyTrip 2.0: a partnership-driven investment model providing working capital support and acquiring up to 49% equity in selected businesses while founders retain full operational control, aimed at diversifying revenue streams.
- Vision 2030: scaling growth across AI-led innovation, international markets, non-air businesses and emerging travel opportunities.
- Accelerate growth across non-air travel verticals (Hotels, Holidays, Visa Services, Airport Services, Duty Free, Experiences) to transition into a diversified travel ecosystem with multiple growth drivers.
- Strengthen the AI-led travel ecosystem and digital capabilities to deliver more intuitive, personalised and seamless travel planning experiences.
- Leverage Dubai as a strategic international hub to support cross-border travel demand and unlock new global opportunities.
- Expand presence across high-growth segments including luxury travel, spiritual tourism, heritage tourism and premium travel experiences.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Spree Hotels, the Company's hospitality management subsidiary, spans 53 properties and 2,222 room keys across cities including Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Goa and Hyderabad, with roughly 31 more properties already signed, and is targeting an expansion to 200 properties over the next five years. YoloBus, the Company's intercity mobility platform, continues to scale under an asset-light model built on partnerships with bus aggregators. Internationally, EaseMyTrip has established operations in the UAE, UK, Thailand, Singapore, the Philippines, New Zealand and the USA, complemented by new wholly-owned subsidiaries in Saudi Arabia and Brazil; the scale-up phase ahead includes further expansion of international offices and subsidiaries, along with regionally tailored product verticals to drive deeper penetration and localisation across each market. The Company has also acquired a 50% stake in Jeewani Hospitality Private Limited, a 49.03% stake in Pflege Home Health Care Center LLC, and made a 49% equity investment in Planet Education Australia Pty Ltd.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's online travel market is expected to grow to USD 36.3 Bn by 2027, positioning the industry for long-term growth and expansion.
- Rising digital penetration, an expanding e-retail landscape, growing disposable income, next-gen online commerce and favourable government measures are structural demand tailwinds for online travel adoption.
- Hotels and Holidays segment growth is being driven by rising demand for experiential, spiritual and leisure travel and personalised offerings, with hotel room-night bookings witnessing robust year-on-year growth.
- International business delivered strong growth during the year, led by the Middle East market and rising travel demand, positioning the Dubai business as one of the strongest-performing international operations within the EaseMyTrip network.

risks.note: Operational and financial performance may be adversely affected by a contraction in the global economy or by disruptions impacting the Indian economy and its travel sector.

The Company is inherently susceptible to seasonal fluctuations within the travel and tourism industry; revenue tends to peak during summer and winter holiday seasons (Q1 and Q3), presenting a recurring challenge to consistent revenue generation.

EaseMyTrip operates within a highly competitive segment of the travel products and services industry, facing rivalry from established online travel agencies, traditional offline travel enterprises, diverse payment platforms, and search engines offering travel-related functionalities.

Significant reliance on airline ticketing as the primary revenue source constitutes a concentration risk; dependence on a single business vertical has the potential to affect revenue stability and margin performance during industry-specific downturns.
The Company faces potential operational challenges should it fail to keep pace with the rapid evolution of technology, which could undermine operational efficiency and overall business performance.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: EaseMyTrip is one of India's leading online travel platforms operating a tri-channel (B2C, B2B2C, B2E) distribution model spanning air, hotels, holidays, rail, bus and ancillary travel services.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: EaseMyTrip commenced operations in 2008 focused on the B2B2C segment, enabling travel agents across India to book domestic airline tickets and serve the offline travel market; it expanded into B2C in 2011 to serve India's growing middle class directly, and into B2E in 2013, offering end-to-end travel management solutions to corporate clients. The platform today offers an end-to-end travel product suite spanning flights, hotels, holidays, trains, buses, charters, cruises, activities, insurance and visas, distributed via websites, mobile apps and a wide travel-agent network, with international operations across the UAE, UK, USA, Singapore, Saudi Arabia and Brazil.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's online travel market is expected to grow to USD 36.3 Bn by 2027, positioning the industry for long-term growth and expansion.
- Rising digital penetration, an expanding e-retail landscape, growing disposable income, next-gen online commerce and favourable government measures are structural demand tailwinds for online travel adoption.
- Hotels and Holidays segment growth is being driven by rising demand for experiential, spiritual and leisure travel and personalised offerings, with hotel room-night bookings witnessing robust year-on-year growth.
- International business delivered strong growth during the year, led by the Middle East market and rising travel demand, positioning the Dubai business as one of the strongest-performing international operations within the EaseMyTrip network.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- EaseMyTrip 2.0: a partnership-driven investment model providing working capital support and acquiring up to 49% equity in selected businesses while founders retain full operational control, aimed at diversifying revenue streams.
- Vision 2030: scaling growth across AI-led innovation, international markets, non-air businesses and emerging travel opportunities.
- Accelerate growth across non-air travel verticals (Hotels, Holidays, Visa Services, Airport Services, Duty Free, Experiences) to transition into a diversified travel ecosystem with multiple growth drivers.
- Strengthen the AI-led travel ecosystem and digital capabilities to deliver more intuitive, personalised and seamless travel planning experiences.
- Leverage Dubai as a strategic international hub to support cross-border travel demand and unlock new global opportunities.
- Expand presence across high-growth segments including luxury travel, spiritual tourism, heritage tourism and premium travel experiences.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
